issues.t: Cracked plastic intake manifold coolant passage
issues.sym: Coolant leaking at the front of the engine near the thermostat housing, a sweet smell, a dropping coolant level and possible overheating.
issues.why: The all-plastic intake manifold's coolant crossover can crack from repeated heating and cooling, and the heater hose and sensor fittings can loosen. Ford changed to an aluminum crossover for 2002.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge and pull over if it rises. Replace the manifold with the updated design.

issues.t: Cruise control deactivation switch can start an underhood fire (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from the engine bay, sometimes even with the car parked and switched off; cruise control may stop working.
issues.why: The cruise control shut-off switch mounted on the brake master cylinder can leak brake fluid internally, overheat and burn. Ford first disconnected the switch, then fitted a fused wiring harness, and recalled some cars again because the first harness was wired with the wrong polarity.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check the VIN for recalls 07V-336 and 08V-051. Until both are done, park away from buildings, and if you see smoke or smell burning, stop and shut the engine off.

issues.sym: All headlights shut off without warning while driving, sometimes coming back after restarting.
issues.why: Solder joints inside the lighting control module crack. After a federal investigation, Ford recalled the cars and replaces the module.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 15V-861 and get the free module. Avoid night driving until it is fixed.

issues.t: Rear wheel bearing and axle shaft wear on police and fleet cars (recall)
issues.sym: Growling or grinding from the rear axle that gets louder with speed. In severe cases an axle can break and a wheel can come loose.
issues.why: Heavy police, taxi and fleet loads overloaded the rear wheel bearings and axle shafts. Ford recalled these cars to replace bearings, seals and shafts.
issues.next: Stop driving if the rear end grinds loudly. Check the VIN for recall 04V-328, especially on ex-police or taxi cars.

issues.t: Steel wheels can crack near the weld (police and taxi)
issues.sym: A tire that keeps losing air, a vibration, or a visible crack around the inner rim of a steel wheel.
issues.why: Steel wheels on police and taxi cars could crack along the weld. Ford recalled certain wheels, added extended coverage, and switched to a stronger wheel.
issues.next: Inspect steel wheels on ex-police or taxi cars and replace any cracked wheel before driving further. Check the VIN for recall 03V-279.

issues.t: Insulation pad can sag onto the catalytic converter (police and taxi recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from under the car or the front floor area, especially after long idling.
issues.why: On police and taxi versions a sound insulating pad can sag in high heat and touch the catalytic converter, which can char it and start a fire. Ford recalled these cars to fit a revised pad.
issues.next: If you see smoke or smell burning, stop and shut the engine off. Have the VIN checked for the open recall on ex-police or taxi cars.

issues.t: Transmission slips from a cracked forward clutch cylinder
issues.sym: Slipping, flaring between gears, delayed engagement or loss of forward drive.
issues.why: The forward clutch cylinder inside the 4-speed automatic can crack. Ford covered the repair under an extended coverage program (06B36).
issues.next: Have the transmission checked promptly and ask a Ford dealer whether the extended coverage was applied to this VIN.

issues.t: Rusted steering shaft can cause loss of steering (recall)
issues.sym: Stiff, notchy or clunking steering, or a steering wheel that suddenly stops controlling the front wheels.
issues.why: Road-salt corrosion can seize the lower intermediate steering shaft, which can collapse the upper shaft and separate the column bearing. Ford recalled cars from salt-belt states, then recalled some again for incorrect repairs.
issues.next: Stop driving if the steering feels unusual. Check the VIN for recalls 13V-385 and 14V-704 and get the free repair.

issues.t: Coolant leak where the intake manifold meets the aluminum crossover
issues.sym: Coolant slowly disappearing, a sweet smell, or wetness and crust at the front of the engine near the thermostat housing. Coolant can pool in the valley under the manifold where it is hard to see.
issues.why: From 2002 Ford added an aluminum coolant crossover to the plastic intake manifold. That cut down on cracking, but the joint between the aluminum and plastic parts tends to seep as the engine ages. The gasket is not sold on its own, so the usual repair is a new manifold.
issues.next: Keep the coolant topped up and watch the temperature gauge. Have the leak confirmed and the manifold replaced before it gets worse, and pull over if the engine starts to overheat.

issues.sym: Slipping, harsh or late shifts, loss of overdrive, or the car not wanting to move in Drive or Reverse.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic is one of the most reported repairs on this car, and a failing front pump is a common cause. Police, taxi and high-idle use add heat and wear.
issues.next: Have the fluid and shifting checked at the first sign of slipping. Continuing to drive a slipping transmission usually turns a smaller repair into a rebuild.

issues.t: Loss of overdrive on police and long-wheelbase taxi cars
issues.sym: The transmission will not shift into overdrive, so the engine revs higher at highway speed.
issues.why: Ford issued service bulletins for police and taxi cars that lose overdrive, with a specific diagnosis and repair procedure.
issues.next: Have a Ford dealer or transmission shop check the bulletins (TSB 17785 and 04163) against the car before replacing parts.

issues.sym: The electronic display in the gauge cluster flickers or blinks.
issues.why: Ford released a service bulletin covering a flickering electronic instrument cluster display on these cars.
issues.next: Mention TSB 17295 to the shop so they follow the published fix.

issues.t: Power window stops working from a worn regulator
issues.sym: A grinding or clicking from inside the door, a window that creeps down or jams part way, or one window that stops moving while the others still work.
issues.why: The plastic parts and cable in the window regulator wear out and let go, so the motor turns but the glass does not move.
issues.next: Get the regulator replaced when a window sticks, especially before winter, since the glass can drop into the door and leave the car open to weather.

issues.t: Front suspension and steering parts wear out
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, wandering or loose steering, uneven front tire wear, and a shimmy you feel through the wheel.
issues.why: Ball joints, stabilizer bar links and the steering idler arm carry a heavy front end and wear out, which lets the front wheels move around.
issues.next: Have the front end inspected and the worn parts replaced; it is a common repair on these cars and it brings the steering and tire wear back to normal.
